The paper analyzes RCS reduction by investigating electromagnetic materials: DPS, DNG, ENG, and MNG.
Transparency conditions are derived by setting the numerator of scattering coefficients to zero.
Resonance conditions are derived by setting the denominator of scattering coefficients to zero.
For TM polarization, transparency occurs when μ = μ_c; resonance occurs when μ = -μ_c.
For TE polarization, transparency occurs when ε = ε_c; resonance occurs when ε = -ε_c.
The study considers an electrically small infinite cylinder with radius 'a' and plane wave incidence.
Both TE and TM polarizations are analyzed for scattering behavior.
Normalized monostatic and bistatic echo widths are used to quantify RCS.
Numerical simulations are performed using Matlab to validate analytical results.
Maximum RCS depends on both incidence and backscattering directions.
MNG and DPS materials are effective for transparency in TM polarization.
ENG and DPS materials are effective for resonance in TE polarization.
Dielectric metamaterials offer advantages such as no metallic loss and isotropic response.
Metallic resonators suffer from conductive loss, narrow bandwidth, and fabrication challenges.
Ohmic losses affect resonance conditions more than transparency conditions.
The incident electric field is expressed in cylindrical coordinates using Bessel and Hankel functions.
The paper uses small-argument approximations of Bessel and Hankel functions for subwavelength conditions.
The study highlights the importance of electric and magnetic dipole moments in metamaterial design.
The RCS can be minimized or maximized by selecting appropriate material parameters and incidence angles.
The work extends previous studies on transparency and resonance in cylindrical and spherical objects.
